title: Estimator Salary: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay for 2026–27
description: Use our estimator salary tool to convert hourly pay to annual, fortnightly and weekly figures. Based on 38 hours, National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading and super.

faqs.q: How do I use the timesheet to estimate my annual salary?
faqs.a: On the timesheet home page, type your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading – do not enter a rate that already includes loading. The tool multiplies your hourly rate by your weekly hours (default 38) and by 52 weeks to show annual gross pay, fortnightly pay, tax withheld, Medicare levy and superannuation.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal floor for award‑free employees. Most workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their classification. Award rates also include penalty rates, allowances and overtime that the National Minimum Wage does not. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides to find the correct award rate for your job.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated in the estimator?
faqs.a: Superannuation is estimated at 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. The calculation stops once your earnings reach the $270,830 maximum contribution base. The estimator shows super as an additional amount, not deducted from your pay. Always check with your employer that the correct super is being paid into your nominated fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## How the estimator salary works

Our [the timesheet](/) converts an hourly rate into annual, fortnightly and weekly figures. The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. We assume a standard full‑time week of 38 ordinary hours, as defined by the Fair Work Commission. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours in the tool.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Multiply by 38 hours gives $1,004.90 per week, and by 52 weeks gives $52,254.80 per year before tax. The tool also shows your fortnightly pay (weekly × 2) and your estimated take‑home pay after tax and Medicare.

### National Minimum Wage vs award rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most Australian workers, however, are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry and classification. Award rates also include penalty rates for weekends, public holidays and overtime, as well as various allowances. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award with the correct minimum pay rates. Always check your award before using a base rate.

### Casual loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. On the timesheet, tick the “casual loading” checkbox and the tool adds 25% to your entered rate. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool applies it for you.

## Tax and Medicare

The estimator uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The tool uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation. The tax estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary sacrifice arrangements. For a more detailed estimate, use the Australian Taxation Office’s gross pay estimator.

## Superannuation

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross salary. The estimator calculates super at 12% and stops once your annual earnings reach the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Super is shown as an additional amount – it is not deducted from your pay. Your employer must pay super into your nominated fund at least quarterly.

## Average weekly earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. That corresponds to an hourly rate of about $54.83 for a 38‑hour week. When all employees (including part‑time) are included, average total earnings were $1,579.20 per week. These figures highlight the difference between award minimums and typical market rates. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more context.

## What the estimator does not include

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) pages, or browse the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) for your award.
